text: Which data structure represents k-mer overlaps as a directed graph and forms the core structure used by many modern genome assembly algorithms?
choices: Adjacency matrix of a hash table
explanation: The de Bruijn graph represents each k-mer's overlaps as edges in a directed graph and is explicitly named as the core data structure for sequence assembly. Suffix trees are instead used for fast exact-match indexing and search rather than assembly graph construction, a binary search tree organizes ordered comparable keys for O(log n) search, and 'adjacency matrix of a hash table' is not a standard structure at all.
